Area.evidence_source: All participants viewed their survival as a re-birth or new beginning. They said that following their suicide attempt, they were able to identify a reason for living. Their suicidal crisis appeared to provide them with an opportunity to reconnect with people close to them and find existential meaning in relationships. For example, Andrew said: One of the things that actually drew me away from that [suicidal behaviour] was just the bible verse of without love we are nothing … The only reason to live is to be there for others. All participants reflected that after their suicide attempt they no longer 'rebelled' against their religion. Two participants broke away from their religion and two participants developed a view of God as caring, rather than punitive. Mark said: 'I believe God is a gentleman. You can do suicide if you want to, but he gives you the alternatives and the ways out.' Engaging in meditation and prayer assisted the participants to rekindle their relationship with God. All participants also remarked that they shifted from being preoccupied with themselves to being aware of others close to them, and the impact the suicide attempt had on these others.
